authoredPrompt: This figure places three small sketched graphs side by side, labeled (a), (b), and (c), each showing curves that rise from left to right on an unmarked vertical axis above a horizontal axis whose tip is labeled n; no numeric ticks appear anywhere. Panel (a) carries three curves: the highest is labeled c2 g(n), the lowest c1 g(n), and a third labeled f(n) weaves between them, dipping and crossing near the left edge before settling into the corridor between the other two. A dashed vertical segment drops from that crossing region to a tick on the n axis marked n0, and the expression f(n) = Theta(g(n)) is printed below the plot. Panel (b) has two curves, the upper labeled c g(n) and the lower labeled f(n); f(n) oscillates sharply at small n, meets c g(n) at the dashed line standing over the tick n0, and runs beneath it from there on, with f(n) = O(g(n)) underneath. Panel (c) reverses the roles, putting f(n) above and c g(n) below after they touch at the dashed n0 line, and is captioned f(n) = Omega(g(n)). Read against one another, the three panels turn on where the labeled curve sits relative to the scaled comparison function once n passes n0, giving the geometric intuition behind bounding a function from both sides, from above only, and from below only.
authoredInteractions:
- Slider for n0: the dashed threshold moves across each plot and violations to its right are marked, making clear that asymptotic bounds only have to hold after a sufficiently large input size.
- Slider for the constant multiplier on g(n): the c g(n), c1 g(n), or c2 g(n) curves move up and down, making clear how constant factors create the allowed upper, lower, or two-sided bound.
- Toggle between Theta, O, and Omega views: the active panel highlights the permitted region for f(n), making clear the difference between two-sided, upper-only, and lower-only comparison.

discrepancies: The three panels are rendered as tiny thumbnails (~100px wide each) pushed to the left edge, whereas the source shows three large, equally-prominent panels filling the full width

The source curves have gentle, irregular undulations; the generated curves use high-frequency sinusoidal oscillations (11–12π cycles) that look like regular sine waves rather than the source's organic wiggles
The source is entirely black-on-white with no fills; the generated figure adds a green shaded corridor and red violation dots, significantly altering the visual character
Inactive panels are dimmed to 32% opacity, whereas the source shows all three panels at equal prominence simultaneously
Curve labels (c₂g(n), f(n), c₁g(n), etc.) are extremely small and nearly illegible at the rendered size due to the compressed panel dimensions
evaluation.notes: The three-panel Θ/O/Ω structure and core asymptotic-notation concepts are correctly implemented with meaningful slider and toggle interactions, but the panels are drastically undersized relative to the viewport, curve oscillations are too regular compared to the source's organic shapes, and the added green shading plus dimmed inactive panels make it look quite different from the clean black-on-white source figure.
action_items: Increase panel width (AW) and reposition panels so the three-panel figure fills at least 80% of the viewBox width, matching the source's balanced three-column layout; reduce or eliminate the right-side whitespace
Reduce the sinusoidal frequency from 11–12π to ~4–5π and add a secondary lower-frequency component so the wiggles look organic like the source rather than like a regular sine wave
Increase all label font sizes (curve labels, n₀, axis label, captions) by at least 40% so they are comfortably readable at inline rendering size
Show all three panels at full opacity in the default state to match the source's simultaneous three-panel presentation; use a subtle highlight border on the active panel instead of dimming the others
